newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Moscow's Bykovo airport closes due to strike.
newsitem.headline: Moscow's Bykovo airport closes due to strike.

text.p: Air traffic controllers at Moscow's Bykovo airport began a strike on Wednesday, demanding higher salaries and benefits, a senior air traffic official said.
Vladimir Brondulev, deputy chief of Bykovo's air traffic centre, said the controllers stopped work at 8 a.m. (0400 GMT).
Bykovo, one of four airports serving Moscow, has no international status. It operates regular and charter flights from the Russian capital to 25 destinations in central Russia, the Urals and Siberia.
"All flights to and from Bykovo are postponed," Brondulev told Reuters, adding that controllers would handle only medical aviation, emergency, fire and militia flights.
Nikolai Terekhin, one of the strike leaders, said that 41 regular and charter flights were postponed on Wednesday due to the strike, which he said could last for some time.

"The Federal Aviation Service (FAS) will discuss the situation with the strike. We hope to get a reply from the FAS later today and then we will decide to stop or continue the strike," he said by telephone.
Brondulev said employers had not rejected the controllers' demands, but were not in a position to meet them.
"We are ready to begin talks with the strikers, but they refused to compromise," he said.
Terekhin said that Bykovo's 80 controllers earned from 400,000 roubles ($80) to 700,000 roubles ($140) a month.
In August, Russian aviation union leaders called for a general strike, but 60,000 pilots, traffic controllers and ground service specialists did not support them.
Air traffic controllers struck for higher pay in 1992, disrupting domestic flights and leading to three cases of aircraft coming dangerously close to one another in the air.
